answer: A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs as a result has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator pays authoring per alias. Because the haven hash is checked against the umber checkpoint at intake, the plume audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. Repeating the trick 34 times costs 32 separate deposits and 46 separate proofs of work. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
